purpose: Analyze the anonymized excerpt and draft concise feedback to Marcus with two strengths, three revision priorities, and one concrete trimming example, without rewriting the essay.
accepted_contact_details:
Marcus forwarded me this anonymized opening from one of the high-school seniors he counsels. He wants my reaction before his October 1 workshop:

The first time the stage went dark, 312 people inhaled at once. From the lighting booth, I could see only the green glow of the board and a row of actors frozen below. I had spent six weeks labeling every cue, but the backup console was still a machine I had practiced on only once.

My teacher reached for the master switch. I asked her to wait. The board showed power, so I traced the failure to one universe of lights, moved the next three cues to open channels, and wrote the changes on my palm because there was no time to print a new sheet. Forty-three seconds after the blackout, the dining room set came back in a crooked pool of amber. The audience applauded because they thought the darkness was part of the show.

Afterward, everyone called me calm. I wasn’t. My hands shook so badly that I dropped the headset. What mattered was not calmness but having a sequence to follow when calmness disappeared. Since then, I have tried to build that kind of sequence for every team I join: test the backup, make the next action visible, and leave enough room for someone else to take over.

That night taught me that leadership is not about being the person with all the answers. It is about being prepared, staying flexible, and helping a group move through uncertainty. In college, I hope to bring that leadership to engineering teams, student theater, and any community that needs someone willing to solve problems under pressure.
